bib.title: Chapter 9: Plotting and Visualization
bib.venue: book chapter (author and edition not printed in the excerpt)

question: How do you make basic exploratory and publication plots in Python with matplotlib, pandas and seaborn?
contributions: A primer on the matplotlib API (figures, subplots, ticks, legends, annotations, patches, saving, rc config)
pandas plotting (line, bar, hist, density, scatter) and seaborn (barplot, distplot, regplot, pairplot, factorplot)

results.claim: Default to matplotlib plus pandas and seaborn for static graphics; Bokeh and Plotly suit interactive web graphics.
results.quote:
For creating static graphics for print or web, I recommend defaulting to matplotlib
and add-on libraries like pandas and seaborn for your needs.

results.claim: Seaborn barplot shows the mean per category with a 95% confidence interval drawn as black lines.
results.quote:
The black lines drawn on the bars represent the 95% confidence interval (this can be
configured through optional arguments).

results.claim: In the tips data, party sizes appear to increase on the weekend (Sat 2-person share 0.623529, Sun 0.520000 vs Fri 0.888889).
results.setup: tips.csv crosstab of day by party size 2-5, rows normalized to sum to 1
results.quote: So you can see that party sizes appear to increase on the weekend in this dataset.

results.claim: Importing seaborn alone changes matplotlib default colors and styles.
results.quote:
Importing seaborn modifies the default matplotlib color schemes
and plot styles to improve readability and aesthetics.

results.claim: Jupyter resets plots after each cell, so complex plots must be built in a single cell.
results.quote:
plots are reset after
each cell is evaluated, so for more complex plots you must put all of
the plotting commands in a single notebook cell.

results.claim: matplotlib does not check for overlapping tick labels; fix by setting ticks and labels explicitly.
results.quote:
matplotlib doesn’t check whether the
labels overlap

limits: Not comprehensive for matplotlib; the author defers to the gallery and docs.

Code dates from the book's era: %matplotlib notebook, sns.distplot, sns.factorplot, sns.set, positional sns.regplot args, AxesSubplot output are deprecated or removed in current seaborn/matplotlib (my note, not the source's).
Examples use random data and a few small CSVs (spx, tips, macrodata) that are not included.
practices: Use the explicit object-oriented API (ax.set_xlim etc.) over pyplot state calls when working with multiple subplots (9.1 Ticks).
Put all plotting commands for a figure in one Jupyter cell (9.1).
Use sharex/sharey when comparing subplots on one scale; otherwise axes autoscale independently (9.1).
Call legend() explicitly; passing label alone does not create it (9.1).
For publication save with dpi and bbox_inches='tight', e.g. plt.savefig('figpath.png', dpi=400, bbox_inches='tight') (9.1).
Use s.value_counts().plot.bar() to show value frequencies (9.2).
Use seaborn when data needs aggregation before plotting (9.2).
Use pairplot for scatter plot matrices in exploratory analysis (9.2).
Use plt.rc or a matplotlibrc file for global defaults (9.1).
